title: Agreement, disagreement and compromise
subtitle: concur with, tally with, dissent, rift, reach a compromise
summary: Use the formal vocabulary of agreeing and disagreeing - concur, tally, accord, dissent, rift, split - and the language of negotiation, from concessions to settlements.

lesson.heading: Agreement: verb + preposition
rows: Her complaints tally with the comments we have received from other people.
match or agree with
His opinion concurs with the general opinion of the experts on this matter.
share/agree with an idea or opinion
The President found herself in full accord with the opposition.
be in complete agreement with
Your views coincide with mine on the question of crime and punishment.
be the same as
His behaviour doesn't conform to the school's expectations.
fit in with
My parents approve of my choice of profession and support me fully.
think something is right or good
lesson.note: Note the prepositions: tally with, concur with, in accord with, coincide with, conform to, approve of.

lesson.heading: Approval and agreeing to differ
lesson.text: The noun from **approve** is **approval**, and an action can **meet with** someone's **approval** - that is, be liked by them. If people continue to hold different opinions but see no point in arguing any longer, they **agree to differ**.

examples.text: We couldn't reach a **consensus** at the meeting, so we just **agreed to differ**.

lesson.heading: Political and social disagreement
rows: There is dissent in the party on the issue.
opposition to the accepted way of thinking
The general discord between the committee members had a negative impact on the club.
lack of agreement or harmony (suggests arguments and rows)
The growing rift in the Democratic Party over defence policy is now public.
disagreement, with different groups or factions forming
A major split in the Labour Party resulted in several ministers forming a new party of their own.
when a larger group breaks up into two or more smaller groups because they disagree
There is major division in the Socialist Party over economic policy.
similar to split but more abstract and formal; can be countable or uncountable
Government plans to build a new airport here are bound to cause controversy.
a lot of disagreement about a subject, usually because it affects a lot of people

lesson.heading: Compromise
lesson.text: Two sides can **reach a compromise**, and a person can **compromise on** an issue - note the preposition. To make a **concession** is to accept some of the other side's demands, and a **settlement** is a decision or agreement that ends a dispute.

examples.text: The two sides have **reached a compromise** over the plan to build the new road across a nature reserve.
The Minister was not prepared to **compromise on** the issue of raising university fees.
The government made several **concessions** to the protesters.
The management and the union **reached a settlement** and the strike ended.

lesson.heading: Discretion
lesson.text: To **exercise discretion** is to be sensitive and use your own judgement about what to say or do. It is a useful formal way of describing tact in a difficult situation.

examples.text: In this particular case, we should **exercise some discretion** and not say anything that would cause more conflict.
You should always **exercise** as much **discretion** as possible when it is a question of people's private lives.

lesson.heading: Agreeing emphatically in conversation
lesson.text: A good way to agree strongly with what someone has just said is simply **Absolutely!** or **Precisely!**

examples.text: *A:* It would be risky to leave your job without getting another one first. *B:* **Precisely!** / **Absolutely!**

lesson.text: Concur, accord and dissent belong to formal writing and news reporting; agree and disagree do the same job in everyday speech.

exercises.prompt: The list of principles ___ to the normal idea of what a set of rules should be trying to achieve.
exercises.explanation: Conform is followed by to: his behaviour doesn't conform to expectations.

exercises.prompt: My views ___ completely with yours. We think on exactly the same lines.
exercises.explanation: Views can tally with or coincide with someone else's - both take with.

exercises.prompt: This plan is in ___ with the proposal made by the committee in 2011.
exercises.hint: (in full ___ with = in complete agreement with)
exercises.explanation: To be in accord with something is to be in complete agreement with it.

exercises.prompt: I ___ of all the changes suggested, and hope they can be made to work.
exercises.explanation: Approve is followed by of: my parents approve of my choice of profession.

exercises.prompt: For once all the committee members ___ with one another.
exercises.explanation: To concur with someone is to share or agree with their opinion; it is quite formal.

exercises.prompt: Even though I disagree, I'm willing to ___ on your proposal to increase our expenditure.
exercises.explanation: You compromise on an issue - note the preposition on.

exercises.prompt: Match each newspaper headline with the extract that goes with it.

pairs.right: There is increasing pressure on the Minister to consider a change to her Party's approach to social welfare.

pairs.left: DISSENT MUST BE KEPT WITHIN LIMITS, MINISTER SAYS
pairs.right: He made the point that to disagree is everyone's right, but a sense of responsibility is also important.

pairs.left: PARTY SPLIT OVER TAX CUTS NO LONGER A SECRET
pairs.right: Approximately 50% of members now think it would have been better to leave things as they were.

pairs.left: DIVISION IN EUROPE OVER RESPONSE TO AFRICAN CRISIS
pairs.right: Several different national approaches have emerged which could weaken unity.
Intolerance towards others' beliefs seems to be increasing and there have been isolated outbreaks of violence.

exercises.prompt: Use a noun: The President made the ___ that the opposition party should be allowed a place on the committee.
exercises.explanation: To make a concession is to accept some of the other side's demands.

exercises.prompt: Use a noun: The landowners reached a ___ in their dispute with the authorities over the proposed factory site.
exercises.explanation: To reach a settlement is to reach a decision or agreement that ends a dispute.

exercises.prompt: Use a noun: The decision to close the railway line has caused a lot of ___ .
exercises.explanation: Controversy is a lot of disagreement about a subject, usually because it affects many people.

exercises.prompt: Use a noun: There is some ___ among the Board members.
exercises.explanation: Dissent is opposition to the accepted way of thinking.

exercises.prompt: Use a noun: Javier's decision met with his parents' ___ .
exercises.explanation: If an action meets with someone's approval, that person likes it.

exercises.prompt: Which noun describes a larger group breaking up into two or more smaller groups because they disagree?
exercises.explanation: A split in a party can result in ministers forming a new party of their own.

exercises.prompt: Your colleague says 'It would be risky to leave your job without getting another one first.' Which one-word reply agrees strongly?
exercises.explanation: Absolutely! and Precisely! are strong ways of agreeing with what someone has just said.

exercises.statement: If two people agree to differ, they have finally reached a consensus.
exercises.explanation: The opposite - they still hold different opinions but see no point in arguing about them any longer.

exercises.prompt: Does each word signal agreement or disagreement?
Put this sentence about negotiation in order.
exercises.answer: The two sides have reached a compromise over the plan
exercises.explanation: You reach a compromise over something, but you compromise on something.
